groups.text: It is currently 18 degrees and mostly clear in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Apple has filed a federal lawsuit in California against OpenAI and two former employees, alleging the misappropriation of trade secrets to aid OpenAI's move into consumer hardware. The suit targets a former vice president of product design for iPhone and Apple Watch, as well as a senior system electrical engineer. Apple claims one defendant used an authentication bug to download confidential hardware files after failing to return a company laptop, while the other emailed himself internal industry summaries and supplier information. Meanwhile, OpenAI reports that its new GPT-5.6 Sol model can independently optimize smaller models. Using a fairly underspecified prompt, Sol autonomously post-trained the Luna model by identifying configurations and selecting GPUs, a task employee Jason Liu says would otherwise take two researchers two weeks. In unrelated news from the UK, police have arrested a 26-year-old man on suspicion of murder following the death of former Tory minister Ann Widdecombe.

Russian airstrikes struck civilian infrastructure in the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia on July 10. Regional governor Ivan Fedorov reports that one person was killed and at least 29 others were injured, including at least one child. Russian forces used guided aerial bombs to damage both residential and non-residential buildings. Police spokeswoman Anna Tkachenko noted that three bombs hit the city, though one remained unexploded in a residential area. Authorities have begun evacuating residents from a damaged apartment building while emergency services continue to respond at the scene. Zaporizhzhia is a major industrial hub located only 20 kilometers from the battlefield, making it a frequent target for Moscow's wide range of weapons. Governor Fedorov has urged residents to stay in safe locations and follow all instructions from police as the response operation continues.

Recent SEC filings show changes in beneficial ownership for two companies across very different sectors. In Fremont, California, Enovix Corporation filed a Form 4 on July 10 regarding reporting by Chakravarthy Arthi. The filing covers a report period ending July 8 and lists the company under miscellaneous electrical machinery and equipment supplies. Meanwhile, J.Jill, Inc., based in Quincy, Massachusetts, also submitted a Form 4 on July 10 for a report period ending July 8. This disclosure involves reporting by Elliot Staples for the women's and juniors outerwear manufacturer. While both companies filed these statements of changes in beneficial ownership on the same day, they operate in unrelated industries. One focuses on electrical equipment manufacturing while the other operates in apparel. These filings provide a factual record of insider ownership shifts but do not indicate a broader connection between the two firms.

NATO leaders have concluded a pivotal summit in Turkey, where President Trump initially questioned the alliance's loyalty before departing in a warmer mood. The gathering focused heavily on Trump's relationship with President Zelensky and the future of Western support for Ukraine. Meanwhile, tensions remain high in the Middle East as Iran held days of public mourning for its late Supreme Leader amid fresh exchanges with the United States that threaten hopes for a lasting ceasefire. In Germany, the Bundestag has passed decisions regarding changes to the heating law and a savings package for statutory health insurance introduced by Health Minister Warken. While some view the reform as a necessary step toward an honest dialogue between healthcare providers and contributors, others warn it could lead to poorer medical care in rural areas. These measures aim to stabilize contribution rates for the insured before a broader health reform begins after the summer break.

Apple has filed a lawsuit against OpenAI in the federal court of Northern California. The computer manufacturer accuses the AI lab of organizing the systematic theft of industrial secrets to speed up the design of future consumer devices. This legal action targets OpenAI, its subsidiary io Products, and two former Apple engineers named Chang Liu and Tang Tan. Io Products is a hardware startup created by former Apple chief designer Jony Ive and acquired by OpenAI in May 2025. The relationship between the two companies has deteriorated sharply despite previous cooperation to integrate ChatGPT into Siri. While Phil Schiller was once considered for an observer seat on OpenAI's board, that partnership never materialized. Now, Apple claims the AI lab used the poaching of its former staff as a method to collect sensitive internal information.

France is facing a growing threat of digital interference as the list of candidates for the 2027 presidential election becomes clearer each week. Experts warn that fake news and online attacks are expected to multiply across the web during this cycle. Nicolas Arpagian, the director of strategy at Jizo AI and a specialist in cybersecurity and digital risk, suggests these challenges create a difficult environment for maintaining electoral integrity. The rise of artificial intelligence further complicates the battle against misinformation and foreign interference. This shift toward high-tech disruption puts pressure on the state to find new ways to protect the democratic process. It remains unclear if the fight against these coordinated online campaigns can be won before voters head to the polls in 2027.

Recent SEC filings from July 10 show changes in beneficial ownership of securities for two major technology firms. At Enovix Corporation, based in Fremont, California, Rajendra K. Talluri filed a Form 4 statement regarding the period ending July 8. This filing comes from a company categorized under miscellaneous electrical machinery and equipment supplies. In a separate action on the same day, Gayla J. Delly filed a similar Statement of Changes in Beneficial Ownership for Broadcom Inc. Based in Palo Alto, California, Broadcom operates within the semiconductors and related devices sector. Both filings were accepted by the SEC on July 10, reflecting ownership shifts that occurred two days prior. These disclosures provide a concrete look at how insiders are managing their holdings within the electrical machinery and semiconductor industries.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with temperatures between 24 and 26 degrees.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
